label: Story
name: story/1
note: A film as one timeline of tracks and clips (play/SPEC.md §12).

node.description: A story is a film as one timeline (format story/1): { schema: 'story/1', format: '9:16' | '16:9' | '1:1' | '4:5', fps: 24 | 25 | 30 | 48 | 50 | 60, duration, tracks }. Each track is { id, kind, clips } and each clip { id, at, duration } in seconds (at may be left out to follow the clip before it), plus its kind's fields: kind 'shots' { frame: an image's hash from add_story_frame (the shot's still), video?: a video's hash from add_story_video (its moving picture, played muted, the story's own sound under it), video_in?: where in the video the shot starts (s), composition?: a composition's hash from add_story_composition (its motion design, one HyperFrames composition played in the shot's place from its 0 at the shot's at, for its length; the frame stays its still), transition: how it goes into the next shot, as code where it starts with one: 'cut', 'dissolve 0.5', 'from black 0.7', 'to black 1', 'dip to black 0.4', several joined by commas ('from black 0.7, cut'), else prose }; kind 'voice' { who, line, cues? } (the narration, shown as the subtitle, cut evenly; or its own subtitles cues: [{ at: seconds into the clip, text, em?: true }], each until the next, em setting one apart, alone and large, such as '100x' while 'a hundred times' is said); kind 'notes' { section, emotion (the one primary emotion the section should leave the viewer with, shown under its name on the timeline), camera, retention, mood } (mood as arrows: ↑ ↑↑ ↑↑↑ ↓ ↓↓ ↕). Any clip of any track may sound: { audio: a recording's hash from add_story_audio, audio_in: where in the recording it starts (s), gain (dB), fade_in, fade_out (s) }, played from the clip's at for its duration; a voice clip's audio is its take, and tracks of kind music, sfx or ambience hold the score, the spot sounds and the beds, their clips overlapping as they like; a track may carry gain (dB) and mute. A clip may carry more fields, and a track may be of another kind (callout, scene): they are kept as given. kind 'story' links other stories in, one clip each: { id, at, story: the linked story's id (a UUID from list_stories, never its title), version: the id of the accepted version of it that plays (get_story's versions) }, that version's whole timeline played in the clip's place from at (its shots, voice, notes and sounds). A link always names its version, so two films may link two versions of one trailer, and a film never changes because the trailer got a new version: moving a film to a newer trailer is a proposal on the film, { op: 'set_clip', track, clip, fields: { version: <the newer version's id> } } (the clip then takes that version's length; shift what follows by the difference if it is longer or shorter). A link's duration is its version's: leave it out and it is given that. A story track's clips never overlap each other, but a linked story may overlap this story's own clips (its music ringing out under the next line). A link is refused without a version, to a story that does not exist, to the story itself, to a version not that story's or never accepted, with a duration other than its version's, and where links would loop (A links B links A) or nest more than 4 stories deep. duration is worked out from the clips. Clip ids are unique within their track; track ids within the story.
